evidence: Reachability is good: Node 22 + express@5.1.0 + better-sqlite3@12.4.1 via NODE_PATH are installed in both environment/Dockerfile and tests/Dockerfile; seed has all 5 accounts, M-11/M-12/M-13, timers [null,1,7,30], Dev walled from M-12, and every seeded fact the criteria rely on (K-10 exactly 7 days old at 2026-05-05T11:00:00Z vs K-11 one second younger; K-1 expired parent with K-14/K-15 replies; held K-17 overdue; K-13 with 2,400 version; K-2 with 'Landlords notice recieved.'; K-16 literal tags). Password, clock, port, DB_PATH, health, env-only start and no-symlink rule are stated in instructions/integration.md and walls-and-retention.md. No browser exists in the agent image, but network is public (SKILL.md delivery profile overrides the Internal sheet's 'no network' wording), so the requested browser self-test is reachable by installing one. Boundary ('as old as its timer' => exactly 7 days gone), edit-does-not-rejuvenate, hold scope, literal search (%,_,*, substring), transcript content, mentions-follow-edits and unread semantics each have one reasonable reading matching the criteria. Defect: walls-and-retention.md:17 requires a plain "not available" only for walled staff and clients reaching matters not theirs, and line 37 says a refused action shows its reason; conversations.md:5 only says nobody can reply across matters, with no refusal form. Yet tests/scored/functional/judge.toml:65-66 (wall_every_route step 5) also replays Dev's reply into M-13, a matter Dev CAN see, and the Fails-if says 'if a refusal is anything but a plain not-available'. That imposes one reading (plain not-available) on a refusal the public text leaves open and arguably steers the other way. The golden happens to return 404 'Not available.' (server.js:407-408), so it is unaffected. Minor note (not a defect): conversations.md 'stay in the order they were sent wherever you see them: ... search' is read by the criterion as oldest-first search (C,A,B); a newest-first search listing would be a weaker second reading, and the golden orders search by seq ascending (server.js:387).
counterexample: A conforming app rejects the JUDGE-W3 replay (Dev, posted to M-11 with parent 'Draft will sent for your review.' from M-13) with HTTP 400 {"error":"A reply has to stay in the matter of the message it answers."} and writes nothing. It satisfies conversations.md:5 and the reason-shown rule of walls-and-retention.md:37, but under wall_every_route's 'if a refusal is anything but a plain not-available' it fails the whole 4.0-weight criterion.
suggested_fix: In wall_every_route step 5/Fails-if, require the plain not-available only for the M-12 (walled) cross reply and accept any refusal that writes nothing for the M-13 cross reply, e.g. 'the JUDGE-W2 replay gets a plain not-available; the JUDGE-W3 replay is refused in any form'.
